analysis: All three changed files are documentation (two new changelog.d entries and an added 'Flint memory admission' section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md). No executable source is in this batch, so no code-level regression can be assessed here. Security-relevant claims in the docs: (1) Flint protocol-constraint state is bounded (maximumStates 8192, 4-entry mask/vocab caches, key bytes 1024, JSON depth 128), with pool exhaustion failing closed as a constraint failure rather than unconstrained generation; this is a DoS/availability-oriented control (T-010, T-029) but the implementation is not supplied. (2) The changelog states the request-normalization identity advances to v9 for all models, so exact-cache entries start cold and providers and coordinators must move to v9 together. That bears on T-041's coordinator-authored cacheSalt, which folds in the prompt-contract ID and block-hash version. A version mismatch would produce cache misses, not cross-scope reuse, so the docs do not suggest weakened isolation. The cache salt derivation and SSD cache code are not shown and need verification in the code PR. (3) Custom stop strings, media and explicit thinking controls are rejected for Flint; this is input-surface hardening whose enforcement is not verifiable from the docs. (4) The claim that the prefill output optimization keeps all trunk work and KV writes is unverifiable here; a bug there would affect output correctness (T-007) rather than confidentiality. (5) The scheduler-prefill fixed-prompt flag is a benchmark-only option with prefix caching disabled, so there is no obvious production exposure. The docs introduce no new endpoints, keys, or trust-boundary changes. Remaining questions for the code-bearing passes are whether Flint tool/reasoning constraint enforcement, the context-limit admission check, and the v9 cache identity are implemented as described. No findings are raised from documentation alone.
